prompt: Complete a TallyCounter class with increment, decrement (which never lets the count drop below zero), reset, and getCount methods.
explanation: The count field is private, so the only ways to change it are the methods the class chooses to expose -- that is what lets decrement enforce the never-below-zero rule reliably. An int field starts at 0 automatically, which covers the initial state without an explicit constructor. Guarding the decrement with a simple if keeps the object's invariant true at all times.
hints: increment is just count++ and reset is count = 0.
In decrement, only subtract when count is greater than 0.
Fields of type int start at 0 by default, so no constructor is required.
